nodes.procedure: Typically, 1.2 mmol of BTC, 1.2 mmol of MA, and 35 mL of methanol were added to a 50 mL capped glass bottle. Then the sealed glass bottle was ultrasonicated for about 2 h until a uniform milky suspension was formed.

nodes.name: NiRu-MOF nanotube synthesis
nodes.procedure: Typically, 2.4 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.15 mmol of RuCl3 were added into the suspension of the HOF nanowire template, followed by a solvothermal treatment at 150°C to drive the HOF-to-MOF transformation process. The mixture was then magnetically stirred for 10 min to obtain a uniform colloidal suspension. Finally, the mixture was transferred into a 50 mL autoclave, heated to 150°C, and kept at this temperature for 12 or 24 h in an airtight environment. The product was separated, rinsed using methanol, and dried in an oven at 60°C.

nodes.procedure: Typically, 1.8 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.15 mmol of MCl3 (M = Ru+Ir) were added into the above formed suspension of HOF template. The mixture was then magnetically stirred for 10 min to obtain a uniform colloidal suspension. Finally, the mixture was transferred into a 50 mL autoclave, heated to 150°C, and kept at this temperature for 12 or 24 h in an airtight environment. The product was separated, rinsed using methanol, and dried in an oven at 60°C.

nodes.procedure: The catalysts were prepared by thermally decomposing the MOF nanotube precursors at 500°C for 4 h under an argon atmosphere in a tubular furnace with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹. The obtained samples were kept in a vacuum drying oven.

nodes.evidence_snippet: the emerged broad peak ranging from 8° - 13° indicates that the NiRu-MOFNTs are in an amorphous state, which is in good agreement with that of the synthesized and also the reported diffraction patterns of NiBTC MOF

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS spectrum shows peaks at 533.1, 532.0, and 531.2 eV assigned to absorbed water, carboxylate groups of BTC linkers, and Ni(Ru)-O bonds respectively. Ni 2p spectrum shows peaks at 856.3 and 873.8 eV for Ni²⁺ 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 with lower binding energy in NiRu-MOFNTs indicating electron transfer from Ru³⁺ to Ni²⁺. Ru 3p peaks at 464.2 and 486.4 eV confirm coordinated Ru³⁺ ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectra (Figure 2g) of Ni-BTC present two intensive peaks at 856.3 and 873.8 eV, which are accordingly identified as the characteristic peaks of Ni²⁺ 2p3/2 and Ni²⁺ 2p1/2, respectively. The Ni 2p binding energy of NiRu-MOFNTs is lower than that of Ni-BTC, indicating that partial electrons transfer from Ru³⁺ to Ni²⁺. As for the chemical binding state of Ru in NiRu-MOFNTs, the binding energy peaks appearing at 464.2 and 486.4 eV are assigned to Ru³⁺ 3p3/2 and Ru³⁺ 3p1/2 (Figure 2h)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals ultrafine metal NCs with mean size of 1.68 nm uniformly distributed on N-doped graphitic nanotubes in NiRuIr@NGTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM (Figure 5d and Figure S27d,e) images revealed that ultrafine metal NCs with a mean size of about 1.68 nm were uniformly distributed on the N-doped graphitic nanotubes

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping confirms large metal NCs are metallic Ni with trace Ru and Ir, while ultrafine metal NCs are RuIr alloy doped with small amount of Ni in NiRuIr@NGTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The images of selected-area EDX elemental mapping and the corresponding EDX spectra (Figure 5g,h and Figure S30) of these two kinds of metal NCs confirmed that the large metal NCs were metallic Ni with trace amounts of Ru and Ir doped, while the ultrafine metal NCs were RuIr alloy doped with a small amount of nickel

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern of NiRuIr@NGTs matches fcc Ni (JCPDS 04-0850) with no obvious reflections for hcp Ru or fcc Ir due to ultrafine features.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PXRD pattern of NiRuIr@NGTs is shown in Figure S32a. All of the diffraction peaks match well with those of fcc Ni (JCPDS card no. 04-0850), while no obvious additional reflections belonging to hcp Ru or fcc Ir were detected

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at ~1583, 1350, and 524 cm⁻¹ assigned to G band, D band, and NiO respectively; high ID/IG ratio indicates highly defective N-doped graphitic carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Several prominent peaks were observed at ∼1583, 1350, and 524 cm⁻¹, which were assigned to the G band of graphitic carbon, the D band of disordered carbon, and NiO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type-IV N2 adsorption-desorption isotherm with H3 hysteresis loop; NiRuIr@NGTs has specific surface area of 118.2 m² g⁻¹ with pore size distribution 2-40 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the NiRuIr@NGTs had a specific surface area of 118.2 m² g⁻¹ with a narrow pore size distribution (inset in Figure S32d) ranging from 2 to 40 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows metallic Ni and surface Ni oxide species. Ru 3d shows metallic Ru and Ru²⁺ coordinated with N/O. Ir 4f shows metallic Ir and oxidized Ir³⁺/Ir⁴⁺ as Ir-O/N. C 1s shows low C-C/C-O ratio (2.8:1) indicating defective carbon. N 1s shows 6.16 at.% N as pyridinic, pyrrolic, and graphitic N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An analysis of the Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure S32e) demonstrated the existence of two different chemical species, metallic Ni and Ni oxide species... two Ru peaks were also resolved from the Ru 3d region (Figure S32f); the lower energy peak was ascribed to metallic Ru... the high-resolution Ir 4f spectrum (Figure S32g) indicated the coexistence of metallic Ir and oxidized Ir (Ir³⁺ and Ir⁴⁺)... The nitrogen content of NiRuIr@NGTs calculated from the N 1s spectrum (Figure S32i) was 6.16 at.%
